Research log.name: panic_day_rebound
Research log.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. Kept the simple rule; protection = size (15% each, 45% total, 3 names). Now trading on paper as strategy #2. | 2026-11-20 round 3 (25 more trials): which 3 to pick barely matters (deepest-under-high +6.0% vs biggest-drop +5.3%, noise); VIX 40+ days best (+9.3%, 85% up, n=13); SECTOR-only panics have no edge (+0.6%), it needs the whole market; fixed 6-day hold best avg, but sell at +10% close or day 6 = +5.0% avg, 72% up, worst -17.5% (vs -21.4%) and frees cash sooner -> adopted. Non-panic swings: best is -10% in 3 days in a calm market, +2.1% over 6d vs +1.0% for any day, steady in both halves (practice candidate only). | 2026-11-23 exits (3 trials, 153 trades on 61 days): sell at +10% on a CLOSE or day 6 = +5.8% avg (71% up) beats a resting +10% limit (+4.4%, 75% up), a +8% limit (+3.7%) and a give-back guard (+5.5%); both halves agree. Winners often run past +10%, so selling intraday cuts them. No change: keep the close rule, no stop (crash-day gaps go straight through stops). | 2026-11-23 sizing (5 trials, $1,000 compounded 2019-2026 incl. 2020 crash): 15%/45% -> $2,248 (10.8%/yr, worst drop -16.5%); 25%/75% -> $3,666 (17.9%, -26.8%); 33%/100% -> $5,023 (22.7%, -34.5%); 50%/100% -> $5,832 (25.0%, -45.2%); 100% one name -> $10,767 (35.1%, -45.5%, only 44 trades: rides on single picks). Every year positive at every size. Owner chose to compound harder: ADOPTED 33% each / 100% total on paper. Panic days are rare (75 of 1,985 sessions), so cash sits idle most days; 3-down-days as an idle-cash setup: +1.66% over 5d vs +0.84% any day, 55% up, too weak alone. | 2026-11-23 adaptive size (13 trials: VIX bands, SPY vs 200d, depth, stock drop; 2 size tables): VIX<25 +7.3% (77% up), VIX 25-40 +2-3% (weakest), VIX 40+ +11.7% (83%); stock -8%+ +7.9% vs -3-5% +3.7%. Steps 10/15/25/40/50% by VIX zone + stock drop: $1,000 -> $5,863 (25.1%/yr, worst drop -23.2%) vs flat 33% $5,018 (-34.5%). Gain is mostly in the older half (newer 1.62x vs 1.64x), so the main win is the smaller drawdown. Same data used to pick the bands: in-sample. ADOPTED with the PM allowed one step up/down after the team talks; each PM size call is scored vs the rule (pm_size_score). | 2026-11-23 intraday caps on top of the close rule (+15/+20/+25% resting sells): +5.2/+5.6/+5.8% vs +5.8% without; no gain, kept as is. Trades that touched +10% intraday but closed below (62 of 153): finished +10.7% avg, 92% up, 66% ended at +10% or more -> holding through that dip is right. | 2026-11-23 profit-lock stops (after a close at +5/+6/+8%, stop at 0/+2/+3%, gap fills at the open): avg +4.8 to +5.3% vs +5.8% without, worst trade unchanged (-27.9%: crash trades never go up first). Not adopted. | 2026-11-23 WIDER UNIVERSE (same rule, $20M+/day and $3+ filter, 0.1% cost, best 3 by depth): nuclear 10: 83 trades +3.45% avg 64% up (older -0.1, newer +6.9); ~74 related stocks: 183 trades +3.95% 66% up (older +2.5, newer +5.4), every year positive; combined 191 trades +3.96%. By group: new nuclear +8.3% (39), AI/data-center +4.3% (131), grid equipment +4.1% (90), mining +3.3% (89), nuclear utilities +2.7% (44), defense +1.6% (36), gas +1.0% (78, worst -62%), builders +0.5% (56). Compounding (adaptive size, cash idle): nuclear only $1,955 (8.9%/yr, -18.7%) vs nuclear first + related fill $2,782 (13.8%/yr, -26.3%). ADOPTED on paper: nuclear picks first, empty slots from the related list. Note: this test's liquidity filter is stricter than the first panic test, so absolute numbers are lower than the earlier 25%/yr; compare within the test.
